correctness.rationale: Condition on B: X_T is Gaussian with integrating-factor mean and variance. Under the scaling B_{Tv}=sqrt(T) times a unit-time Brownian path in law, physical backward lag y/T becomes y/T² in that path. For G≠0 the last fixed fraction of the unit path is bounded away from zero, giving an integrable exponential majorant on the corresponding y-range and a negligible T²-exp(-const*T²) tail. This yields TV_T→D/(bG²) and vanishing scaled initial mean on the scaling coupling, including a=0. Future W increments form a standard Brownian driver independent of the initial data; the environmental increment divided by sqrt(T) has squared uniform norm O_P(T^-2). With nonnegative drift, integration by parts bounds the convolution by twice the driver supremum. The drift difference bound can be taken as H times the uniform coefficient error times the tight solution supremum. The resulting continuous frozen solution map proves convergence in C([0,H]), not just of marginals. The conditioned Gaussian pair is stationary with correlation exp(-bG²u); no axis atoms obstruct weak convergence of the sign product, including u=0. Rescale g by sqrt(bu), use dominated convergence, and integrate the nonnegative arcsine series termwise. Independent 60-digit quadrature, integrating by parts after exp(-y²)=sin(theta), reproduces K=0.5388516236620413677555756… . The heavy tail and nonintegrability concern the sequential limiting sign process only.
residual_risks: No moment or growing-window convergence; the limiting spatial Cauchy marginal has no variance.
